html:
The Ungazigmit are a Yupik people of the eastern tip of the Chukchi Peninsula in Russia, named after their old village of Ungaziq at Cape Chaplino, facing Alaska across the Bering Strait. They speak Central Siberian Yupik, the same language as the St. Lawrence Island Yupik of Alaska.

They hunted walrus, seals and whales from skin boats and kept close ties with relatives across the strait. In Soviet times their old village was closed and its people moved to a new settlement. Their neighbours inland were the reindeer herding Chukchi.
